## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:
```{r}
# Clear environment
rm(list = ls())

# Load packages
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(emmeans)
library(multcomp)
library(writexl)

# Read data
setwd("~/Desktop/codes")
dat <- read_excel("~/Desktop/codes/data/Sp_Table1.xlsx", sheet = "Sheet1")

# Factor settings
dat$Nadd   <- factor(dat$Nadd, levels = c("Ncont", "Ncess"))
dat$Nlevel <- factor(dat$Nlevel, levels = c("N0","N02","N05","N10","N15","N20","N50"))
dat$Block  <- factor(dat$Block)

# ==================== Analysis for pH ====================
analyze_pH <- function(data, group_name, letter_type) {
  model <- aov(pH ~ Nlevel + Block, data = data)
  emm   <- emmeans(model, "Nlevel")
  cl    <- cld(emm, Letters = letters, adjust = "tukey", reversed = TRUE)  # ← Tukey
  
  letters_df <- as.data.frame(cl) %>% dplyr::select(Nlevel, .group)
  
  stats <- data %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Nlevel) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      Mean = round(mean(pH, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      SE   = round(sd(pH, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()), 3),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  dplyr::left_join(stats, letters_df, by = "Nlevel")
}

# ==================== Run analysis ====================
res_Ncont <- dat %>% dplyr::filter(Nadd == "Ncont") %>% analyze_pH("Ncont", letters)
res_Ncess <- dat %>% dplyr::filter(Nadd == "Ncess") %>% analyze_pH("Ncess", letters)

# ==================== Combine results ====================
res_Ncont$Nadd <- "Ncont"
res_Ncess$Nadd <- "Ncess"

final <- dplyr::bind_rows(res_Ncont, res_Ncess) %>%
  dplyr::select(Nadd, Nlevel, Mean, SE, .group) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Letter = .group)

# View results
print(final, n = Inf)

# Export to Excel
write_xlsx(final, "~/Desktop/codes/tables/Sp_table1_pH.xlsx")
cat("\n✅ Analysis completed! Results exported successfully.\n")
```
